title: Indoor air purifiers and HEPA filtration
text: An indoor air purifier with a HEPA filter removes fine particulate matter from a single room. Run it in the bedroom at night and keep doors closed for the best reduction in indoor PM2.5.

title: Ventilation timing on high pollution days
text: Open windows early in the morning or late at night when outdoor PM2.5 is lower. Avoid ventilating during traffic peaks and stubble-burning episodes.

title: Cooking emissions and kitchen exhaust
text: Cooking with solid fuels such as wood, coal and kerosene releases smoke and fine particles. Use a kitchen exhaust fan, cover pans and prefer LPG, PNG, biogas or electric cooking.

title: Low emission commuting choices
text: Walking, cycling, metro and bus travel emit far less per passenger kilometre than a private car. Combining a short cycle ride with metro travel cuts weekly commute emissions substantially.

title: Do not burn waste or dry leaves
text: Open burning of garden waste, dry leaves and rubbish releases dioxins and thick smoke. Compost green waste instead and dispose of plastic through municipal collection.

title: Protecting children and the elderly
text: Children and older adults breathe more air per body weight and are more vulnerable to PM2.5. Keep them indoors on Poor, Very Poor and Severe days and avoid school-run exposure during smog episodes.

title: Respiratory conditions and air quality
text: People with asthma or COPD should follow their action plan, keep reliever medication nearby and reduce exertion outdoors when the AQI is above 200.

title: Understanding CPCB AQI bands
text: The CPCB AQI bands are Good (0-50), Satisfactory (51-100), Moderately Polluted (101-200), Poor (201-300), Very Poor (301-400) and Severe (401-500). Each band carries a different health advisory.

title: Indoor plants and air quality
text: Houseplants improve comfort but remove particulate matter only in a small way. They are not a substitute for ventilation control, exhaust fans or a HEPA air purifier.

title: Masks for smog and commute
text: A well fitted N95 or N99 mask filters fine particles during travel on high pollution days. Cloth and surgical masks do not seal well enough to protect against PM2.5.
